chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has ruled regarding your blood differently from how He has ruled regarding your wealth. He ruled concerning your wealth that the proof is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made; and He ruled concerning your blood that the oath is upon the claimant and the proof is upon the one against whom the claim is made, so that the blood of a Muslim man may not be nullified.

key_terms.أَمْوَالِكُمْ: your wealth, meaning property and financial claims
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: the evidentiary proof presented in a legal claim
key_terms.الْيَمِينَ: the oath sworn in judicial procedure
key_terms.دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: the blood of a Muslim person, i.e. protected life under the law
key_terms.دِمَائِكُمْ: your bloods, meaning cases involving bloodshed or homicide

ai.seo_question: How does Islamic law distinguish between claims about wealth and claims about bloodshed?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal distinction between claims involving property and claims involving bloodshed. In financial disputes, the claimant must produce proof, whereas in blood cases the procedure differs in order to safeguard life and prevent the blood of a Muslim from being left without due legal protection.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5175 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has ruled differently regarding your blood than He (swt) has regarding your wealth.
In matters of wealth, the ruling is that the burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.
However, in matters of blood, the ruling is that the oath is upon the claimant, and the proof is upon the one against whom the claim is made, so that the blood of a Muslim is not unjustly nullified."
